summary: Feed s171_triple is degraded: 3 faults found. IDS requires both directions, full payload, and VLANs 10,20. Detected 76.3% one-way sessions, 100% untagged (VLANs 10,20 missing), and 75.1% encrypted traffic exceeding 60% tolerance. No duplicates, drops, or overload detected.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker or TAP/SPAN is stripping 802.1Q tags upstream - 100% of packets are untagged while VLANs 10 and 20 are required. Likely broker port set to strip tags or mirror taken from untagged access port.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS cannot apply VLAN-aware policies or segment detection for VLANs 10 and 20; traffic from those segments is invisible or misclassified, creating complete coverage gap for those VLANs.

recommended_fix.why: Restore and preserve 802.1Q tags for VLANs 10 and 20 through the packet broker to the IDS so it can filter and detect per-segment as required.

findings.root_cause: Only one direction of 87 of 114 TCP sessions (76.3%) reaches the IDS. Indicates asymmetric routing with unaggregated TAPs or SPAN configured for single direction, or broker hashing directions to different tool ports without aggregation.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs both directions for stateful TCP reassembly and signature matching. One-way visibility causes missed handshakes, broken flow reconstruction, false negatives and inability to detect bidirectional attacks.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregate both directions of each session at the packet broker and deliver the complete bidirectional flow to the same IDS tool port to restore stateful inspection.

findings.root_cause: 75.1% of bytes are encrypted (TLS/encrypted), exceeding IDS tolerance of 60%. Traffic is predominantly encrypted and delivered as ciphertext with no upstream decryption.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs full payload for signature and anomaly detection but is blind to encrypted payloads; detection reduces to metadata only, significantly lowering detection coverage for this IDS.

recommended_fix.why: Advise decrypting relevant TLS at packet broker / dedicated decryption zone or selectively filtering/bypassing trusted encrypted flows so IDS receives inspectable payload within its tolerance.
